question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded bet-hedging profiling
ideas.description: Borrowing portfolio diversification from finance, label the parental line with a high-complexity lentiviral barcode library, then use scRNA-seq to profile barcoded cells before and early during drug exposure. Test whether survivor barcodes are enriched for pre-existing transcriptional states (a pre-positioned hedge) rather than being randomly distributed or induced by the drug.

ideas.title: Frailty survival modeling of live single-cell reporters
ideas.description: Borrowing burn-in and frailty models from reliability engineering, track individual cells under continuous drug with a live reporter combining cell-cycle (FUCCI) and stress-pathway biosensors, recording time to death. Fit Cox or frailty models against pre-treatment reporter levels and lineage history; a heavy-tailed hazard distribution would indicate a subpopulation with intrinsically lower hazard.

ideas.title: Early-warning signals of a drug-induced tipping point
ideas.description: Borrowing critical slowing down from ecological and climate tipping-point theory, collect time-series single-cell expression data during low-dose drug exposure and track rising variance and lag-1 autocorrelation of key transcripts as a predictor of a bistable switch into the persister state. Validate causally by perturbing noise (for example, pulsed drug or heat shock) and checking whether the persister fraction shifts accordingly.

ideas.title: Re-challenge recall assay for tolerance memory
ideas.description: Borrowing the immunological recall test from vaccine research, sort surviving cells, expand them drug-free for multiple passages, and then re-challenge with drug. Track whether tolerance decays (indicating reversible, epigenetically or transcriptionally maintained memory) or persists (suggesting a stable heritable state), profiling chromatin accessibility by ATAC-seq at each stage to map the memory's regulatory basis.

ideas.title: Spatial refugia mapping in 3D tumor models
ideas.description: Borrowing the habitat-refugia concept from ecology, combine multiplexed spatial imaging (MERFISH or CODEX) with a drug-penetration readout such as a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging in spheroids or tumor sections. Test whether persisters cluster in low-drug, hypoxic, or cell-contact-protected niches, and whether their transcriptional state tracks the local microenvironment rather than an intrinsic property.
